observations.evidence: On the left, a yellow longitudinal edge line runs along the kerb of a planted grass median (from bottom-left about x 0-60, y 470-500 toward x 220, y 340). Beyond the median at far left is the opposing carriageway. This is the left limit of the EB carriageway at this cross-section.

A solid white longitudinal line runs from about (315, 640) at the bottom up to about (290, 360). It separates the camera's motor-vehicle strip, between the yellow edge line and this line, from a bicycle lane to its right. At this position only one motor-lane-width strip is visible between the yellow line and this white line.

A bicycle lane lies immediately right of the solid white line. Where it crosses the crosswalk in front of the camera (about x 290-430, y 425-535) it is painted green, with short dashed white edge lines. A second green patch is visible further ahead (about x 290-320, y 350-360). No bicycle symbol is legible in this view.
Right of the bicycle lane, a chevron-hatched painted buffer (about x 325-405, y 360-430) is bounded by white lines. It is widest nearest the camera and tapers to a point further ahead.

Between the hatched buffer and the right kerb (about x 400-580, y 360-470) there is a paved kerbside strip with a storm-drain grate and no lane markings or vehicles. A shuttle/bus-stop sign stands on the adjacent sidewalk. Whether this strip is a bus stop, parking or loading zone, or a travel lane cannot be determined from the image.
Pole at the right kerb (about x 600-615, y 255-345) with a transit/shuttle stop sign (bus pictogram) and red-and-white regulatory plates below it. The plate text is not readable at this resolution.

In the near field the camera stands just before a faded, patched crosswalk (y about 480-570) crossing the whole EB carriageway, with a transverse white stop line at bottom right (about x 470-640, y 585-600). This is an upstream crossing about 100 m from the junction centre, not the target approach's stop bar.

Further downstream, a white longitudinal line appears within the motor carriageway (about x 255-258, y 337-356), with a short transverse white mark to its right (about x 262-278, y 346). This may mark an added lane or lane split closer to the junction, but it is too distant and small to confirm.

Downstream on the right, street trees and a raised kerb/planter area beside the bicycle lane (about x 300-340, y 330-355) partly hide the kerbside layout near the junction. An orange diamond warning sign (about x 322-334, y 293-307) is unreadable. Distant pavement near the junction is too low-resolution to read markings.

notes: No pavement arrows (left, through, right or U-turn) are visible anywhere in this view, near or far.
The view describes the upstream cross-section about 100 m from the junction centre. Turn pockets or lane additions near the stop bar (see o8) cannot be read from this image.
YOLO hints: the 'person' box matches a pedestrian with a dog on the right sidewalk. The 'car' boxes are distant vehicles near the junction. None occlude the near pavement.
Capture date 2020-11 (as supplied). The layout may differ in newer imagery.
